I Bet This Is Happening In Alberta Too

Jul 27, 2007 • Janice Cotcher

I have a serious issue with standardized testing, especially the way most governments treat standardize testing. Standardize testing should be used as a diagnostic tool, no more than that. When teachers’ jobs depend on the result of their students, this is what happens:
Teachers cheating to raise grades By Penny Haslam, BBC News, Five Live Report
I’ve heard rumours of administrators doctoring marks also.

Author: Teacher Lady
Date: 2007-07-28 17:31:00

>Your teacher’s job and the reputation of the school were not riding on the results of your standardized tests. Standardized tests are good for knowing approximately what grade level a student is at. They are meant to compare students to a standard then use that information to help them. It is unfair when you start comparing students to each other, classes to each other and schools to each other.Think of it this way, would it be fair to compare an English 30 class from Scott to an English 30 class at Campbell? Absolutely not. You need students from the exact same cultural and soci-economical background to have fair comparison. Unfortunately this is what is happening in Alberta, the UK and most of the Western world.Yees dear, you’re awesome. Realize that yours is not the common experience.
